criteriaCodes.label: BP6

criteriaCodes.description:
Co-segregation with disease in multiple affected family members in a gene definitively known to cause the disease.
Note: May be used as stronger evidence with increasing segregation data.

evidenceStrengths.description:

*   Co-segregation with disease phenotype in multiple affected family members: 
    *   \*3 affected homozygotes/compound heterozygotes + 0 Unaffected homozygous/compound heterozygotes.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

criteriaCodes.label: PP1

criteriaCodes.description:
Novel missense change at an amino acid residue where a different missense change determined to be pathogenic has been seen before.
Example: Arg156His is pathogenic; now you observe Arg156Cys.
Caveat: Beware of changes that impact splicing rather than at the amino acid/protein level.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Moderate 2 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Novel missense change at amino acid residue where a different missense change is determined to be pathogenic in at least 1 case, where a different missense change is determined to be pathogenic in at least 1 case as determined by the _DDC_ VCEP or curated using these _DDC_ specifications in the absence of applying PM5 for that variant (or similar).
*   Likely pathogenic variant as determined by VCEP at the residue in **≥2** cases.
    *   Caveat – Beware of changes that impact splicing rather than at the amino acid/protein level.
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Supporting 1 point per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Likely pathogenic variant as determined by VCEP at the residue in only one case.
    *   Caveat - Consider changes that impact splicing rather than at the amino acid/protein level
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PM5

criteriaCodes.description: Allele frequency is greater than expected for disorder.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Strong 4 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Any variant with a frequency>0.002 (0.2%) (based on the estimated prevalence of 1 in 90,000 in gnomAD (max allelic contribution = 44%; max genetic contribution = 100%) will meet strong benign criteria.
*   Use the highest population minor allele frequency in any given continental population with >2,000 alleles (European non-Finnish, African, East Asian, South Asian, Latino) (PMID 20211383)
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

criteriaCodes.label: BS1

criteriaCodes.description: Missense variant in a gene that has a low rate of benign missense variation and where missense variants are a common mechanism of disease.
criteriaCodes.label: PP2

criteriaCodes.description:
The prevalence of the variant in affected individuals is significantly increased compared to the prevalence in controls.
Note 1: Relative risk (RR) or odds ratio (OR), as obtained from case-control studies, is >5.0 and the confidence interval around the estimate of RR or OR does not include 1.0. See manuscript for detailed guidance.
Note 2: In instances of very rare variants where case-control studies may not reach statistical significance, the prior observation of the variant in multiple unrelated patients with the same phenotype, and its absence in controls, may be used as moderate level of evidence.
criteriaCodes.label: PS4

criteriaCodes.description: Located in a mutational hot spot and/or critical and well-established functional domain (e.g. active site of an enzyme) without benign variation.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Moderate 2 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Located in a mutational hot spot and/or critical and well-established functional domain (e.g., active site of an enzyme) without benign variation.
*   Suggested hotspots (Bisello et al, 2023, PMID:37466248): 
    *   1\. HS: c.439-447; p.Ser147-p.Ser149 (PLP binding)
    *   2\. HS: c.574-576; p.His192 (PLP-binding)
    *   3\. HS: c.714+4A>T /IVS6+4A>T  (founder variant)
    *   4\. HS: c.811-813; p.Asp271 (PLP binding)
    *   5\. HS: c.907-909 ; p.Lys303 (PLP binding)
    *   6\. HS: c.979-1071; p.Arg327-p.Phe357 (catalysis)
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

criteriaCodes.label: PM1

criteriaCodes.description: Assumed de novo, but without confirmation of paternity and maternity.
criteriaCodes.label: PM6

criteriaCodes.description: Variant found in a case with an alternate molecular basis for disease.
criteriaCodes.label: BP5

criteriaCodes.description: Observed in a healthy adult individual for a recessive (homozygous), dominant (heterozygous), or X-linked (hemizygous) disorder, with full penetrance expected at an early age.

evidenceStrengths.description:
**(Strong 4 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**

*   The patient must have normal DDC enzyme activity in order to apply this criterion.
*   Exception to this rule applies for hypomorphic variants, which are benign in the homozygous state but can cause disease/clinically relevant enzyme deficiency when in trans with a severe deleterious variant. It is presently not possible to set activity range for individuals homozygous for hypomorphic alleles.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

criteriaCodes.label: BS2

criteriaCodes.description:
For recessive disorders, detected in trans with a pathogenic variant
Note: This requires testing of parents (or offspring) to determine phase.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Very Strong 8 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Can only be used in connection with PM2\_supporting. 
    *   \*4 points awarded from Table 1 (See attached Ellard et al., 2020; [https://www.acgs.uk.com/media/11631/uk-practice-guidelines-for-variant-classification-v4-01-2020.pdf](https://www.acgs.uk.com/media/11631/uk-practice-guidelines-for-variant-classification-v4-01-2020.pdf) )
evidenceStrengths.label: Very Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Strong 4 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Can only be used in connection with PM2 supporting.
*   Follow SVI guidance for PM3 - \*2 points awarded from table 1(See attached Ellard et al., 2020; https://www.acgs.uk.com/media/11631/uk-practice-guidelines-for-variant-classification-v4-01-2020.pdf ). e.g., Detected in trans in 2 probands with a pathogenic variant (recessive)
*   \*Not more than 2 homozygotes to be used points calculations for PM3\_Strong
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Moderate 2 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Follow SVI guidance for PM3 - \*1 point awarded from table 1(See attached Ellard et al., 2020; https://www.acgs.uk.com/media/11631/uk-practice-guidelines-for-variant-classification-v4-01-2020.pdf ). e.g., Detected in trans in 1 probands with a pathogenic variant (recessive)
*   \*Not more than 2 homozygotes to be used points calculations for PM3\_Moderate
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Supporting 1 point per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Can only be used in connection with PM2 supporting.
    *   \*\*\*\*\*0.5 points awarded from table 1(See attached Ellard et al., 2020) e.g., Two variants that meet PM2\_Supporting detected in trans: OR a homozygous variant meeting PM2\_Supporting
    *   PM2\_supporting must be met for PM3\_moderate - with the exception of known hypomorphic alleles. A PMID is not available for Ellard, et al. 2020. This document can be found at: [https://www.acgs.uk.com/media/11631/uk-practice-guidelines-for-variant-classification-v4-01-2020.pdf](https://www.acgs.uk.com/media/11631/uk-practice-guidelines-for-variant-classification-v4-01-2020.pdf)
    *   Unless the variant under assessment is a known hypomorphic allele, homozygotes present in population databases should not be acceptable for the application of PM2\_Supporting. Will include hypomorphic alleles in pilot phase to develop more clear guidelines. (Bisello et al., 2024, PMID: 39166734; Bisello & Bertoldi., 2022, PMID: 36232540).
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PM3

criteriaCodes.description: Well-established in vitro or in vivo functional studies show no damaging effect on protein function or splicing.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Supporting 1 point per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   In vitro activity >60%
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: BS3

criteriaCodes.description:
Same amino acid change as a previously established pathogenic variant regardless of nucleotide change.
Example: Val->Leu caused by either G>C or G>T in the same codon.
Caveat: Beware of changes that impact splicing rather than at the amino acid/protein level.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Strong 4 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)** 
*   Same amino acid change as a previously established **(likely)** pathogenic variant must reach a classification of LP without PS1 using these DDC specifications. 
*   Initiation codon variants where a different nucleotide substitution affecting the initiation codon has been classified as pathogenic.
*   Splicing variants where a different nucleotide substitution has been classified as a **pathogenic** and the variant being assessed is predicted by _in silico_ tools to have a similar or greater deleterious impact. 
*    Consider  nucleotide changes that impact splicing rather than at the amino acid/protein level
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

criteriaCodes.label: PS1

criteriaCodes.description: Observed in trans with a pathogenic variant for a fully penetrant dominant gene/disorder or observed in cis with a pathogenic variant in any inheritance pattern.
criteriaCodes.label: BP2

criteriaCodes.description: Missense variant in a gene for which primarily truncating variants are known to cause disease.
criteriaCodes.label: BP1

criteriaCodes.description:
De novo (both maternity and paternity confirmed) in a patient with the disease and no family history.
Note: Confirmation of paternity only is insufficient. Egg donation, surrogate motherhood, errors in embryo transfer, etc. can contribute to non-maternity.
criteriaCodes.label: PS2

criteriaCodes.description: In frame-deletions/insertions in a repetitive region without a known function.
criteriaCodes.label: BP3

criteriaCodes.description:
Well-established in vitro or in vivo functional studies supportive of a damaging effect on the gene or gene product.
Note: Functional studies that have been validated and shown to be reproducible and robust in a clinical diagnostic laboratory setting are considered the most well-established.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Moderate 2 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   in vitro activity \< 10% in non-patient derived cells or in solution.
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Supporting 1 point per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   in vitro activity \< 45% in non-patient derived cells or in solution **OR** totally insoluble variants in bacterial or eukaryotic cells (only recovered in the pellet)
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PS3

criteriaCodes.description:
Multiple lines of computational evidence suggest no impact on gene or gene product (conservation, evolutionary, splicing impact, etc)
Caveat: As many in silico algorithms use the same or very similar input for their predictions, each algorithm cannot be counted as an independent criterion. BP4 can be used only once in any evaluation of a variant.

evidenceStrengths.description:
For splice site variants use SpliceAI. BP4 can be applied if there is a SpliceAI “low score” (delta score ≤0.2 “predicted to alter splicing”).

Due to some pathogenic variants having low REVEL scores, BP4 is not applied for missense variants.
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: BP4

criteriaCodes.description:
Lack of segregation in affected members of a family.
Caveat: The presence of phenocopies for common phenotypes (i.e. cancer, epilepsy) can mimic lack of segregation among affected individuals. Also, families may have more than one pathogenic variant contributing to an autosomal dominant disorder, further confounding an apparent lack of segregation.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Strong 4 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Lack of segregation in affected members of a family. Follow SVI guidance.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

criteriaCodes.label: BS4

criteriaCodes.description:
Absent from controls (or at extremely low frequency if recessive) in Exome Sequencing Project, 1000 Genomes or Exome Aggregation Consortium.
Caveat: Population data for indels may be poorly called by next generation sequencing.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Supporting 1 point per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Will **NOT** be used at moderate strength.
*   Only applied as a Supporting criterion
    *   \<0.02%, 0.0002
        *   an order of magnitude below the BS1 threshold
*   Unless the variant under assessment is a known hypomorphic allele, homozygotes present in population databases should not be acceptable for the application of PM2\_Supporting. Will include hypomorphic alleles in pilot phase to develop more clear guidelines. (Bisello et al., 2024, PMID: 39166734; Bisello & Bertoldi., 2022, PMID: 36232540).
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PP5

criteriaCodes.description: Protein length changes due to in-frame deletions/insertions in a non-repeat region or stop-loss variants.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Moderate 2 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Use for in frame deletions and insertions of 2 or more amino acid.
*   e.g., PM4\_moderate:c.270\_281dup; p.Ala91\_Leu94dup
*   PM4 cannot be used together with PVS1.
*   Stop loss variants in _DDC_ have not been reported, as far as we are aware.
*   PM4 classification for stop loss variants should be made according to previously published decision tree (Ellard et al. 2020) (See attached)
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Supporting 1 point per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Use for in frame deletions and insertions is a single amino acid
*   e.g., PM4\_supporting: c.58\_60del; p.Tyr20del
*   PM4 cannot be used together with PVS1
*   Stop loss variants in _DDC_ have not been reported, as far as we are aware
*   PM4 classification for stop loss variants should be made according to previously published decision tree (Ellard et al. 2020) (See attached)
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PM4

criteriaCodes.description: Allele frequency is above 5% in Exome Sequencing Project, 1000 Genomes or Exome Aggregation Consortium.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   A “stand-alone” criterion -10 points - automatically classified as benign.
*   An allele frequency of ≥0.004 (0.4%) in any continental population in gnomAD v2.1.1 or v4.0 with >2000 alleles as a cutoff for stand-alone benign criteria which is calculated using 100% genetic heterogeneity, because _DDC_ variants are the only known genetic cause of AADC deficiency, and full penetrance.
evidenceStrengths.label: Stand Alone

criteriaCodes.label: BA1

criteriaCodes.description:
Multiple lines of computational evidence support a deleterious effect on the gene or gene product (conservation, evolutionary, splicing impact, etc.).
Caveat: As many in silico algorithms use the same or very similar input for their predictions, each algorithm should not be counted as an independent criterion. PP3 can be used only once in any evaluation of a variant.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Supporting 1 point per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Missense variants with REVEL >0.55, we suggest  ≥0.55: lowest REVEL score likely pathogenic variants is 0.552, p.Val68Met  (Himmelreich et al 2022, PMID: 36427457)
*   Predicted impact on splicing by SpliceAI not in classical splicing.
*   For canonical splice site variant, the cut-off for SpliceAI is 0.5
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PP3

criteriaCodes.description: A synonymous variant for which splicing prediction algorithms predict no impact to the splice consensus sequence nor the creation of a new splice site AND the nucleotide is not highly conserved.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Strong 4 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Silent substitutions that are absence of experimentally observed splicing impacts (Walker et al., AJHG 2023, PMID 37352859)
    *   Only apply if BP4 is met.
    *   Evolutionary conservation is not considered informative for application of this code.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Supporting 1 point per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Synonymous (silent) variant with low prior probability of pathogenicity if no predicted impact on splicing. SpliceAI \<0.2, no predicted impact on splicing, as per BP4.
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: BP7

criteriaCodes.description:
Null variant (nonsense, frameshift, canonical +/−1 or 2 splice sites, initiation codon, single or multi-exon deletion) in a gene where loss of function (LOF) is a known mechanism of disease.
Caveats:
 * Beware of genes where LOF is not a known disease mechanism (e.g. GFAP, MYH7).
 * Use caution interpreting LOF variants at the extreme 3’ end of a gene.
 * Use caution with splice variants that are predicted to lead to exon skipping but leave the remainder of the protein intact.
 * Use caution in the presence of multiple transcripts.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   **(Very Strong 8 points per Bayesian framework, Tavtigian, et al. 2018, PMID:** **29300386)**
*   Cannot be used together with PM4 or PP3
*   If there's a stop loss variant, then PM4 is to be considered.
*   Classifications should be made according to a decision tree (See attached) (Based on Tayoun et al., 2018)
